title: St. Francis de Sales Examination of Conscience
description: A gentle but thorough examination focusing on everyday virtues and habits, based on the spirituality of St. Francis de Sales and his 'Introduction to the Devout Life'.

categories.title: Relationship with God
categories.description: St. Francis de Sales emphasized that devotion consists in doing ordinary actions with extraordinary love for God.

items.text: Have I failed to make time for daily prayer and meditation?
items.clarification: St. Francis taught that even 15 minutes of meditation each day can transform our spiritual life.

items.text: Have I prayed merely out of habit, without attention or love?
items.clarification: The saint advised, 'It is better to say one Our Father with devotion than many without attention.'

items.text: Have I neglected to offer my daily actions to God?
items.clarification: St. Francis encouraged offering each day and all its activities to God each morning.

items.text: Have I failed to seek God's presence throughout my day?
items.clarification: Francis advised frequently recalling God's presence during ordinary activities.

items.text: Have I neglected to thank God for His blessings and graces?
Have I doubted God's love for me or His providence in my life?
Have I approached the sacraments without proper preparation or thanksgiving?
Have I been lukewarm in my devotion to God?
Have I neglected spiritual reading that would nurture my faith?
Have I been silent about my faith when I should have spoken up for it?

categories.title: Gentleness and Humility
categories.description: Central virtues in St. Francis de Sales' spirituality are gentleness (particularly with ourselves) and humility.

items.text: Have I been harsh or impatient with myself when I've made mistakes?
items.clarification: St. Francis particularly emphasized being gentle with ourselves: 'Be patient with everyone, but above all with yourself.'

items.text: Have I been impatient or irritable with others?
items.clarification: He advised, 'Nothing is so strong as gentleness, nothing so gentle as real strength.'

items.text: Have I given in to anger or acted with harshness towards anyone?
Have I spoken unkindly or raised my voice unnecessarily?
Have I been prideful or arrogant, considering myself better than others?
Have I sought praise or recognition for my actions?
Have I been unwilling to acknowledge my faults or accept correction?
Have I been overly concerned with what others think of me?
Have I allowed anxiety, frustration, or discouragement to prevail over trust in God?

categories.title: Charity Towards Neighbor
categories.description: St. Francis taught that our love for God should be expressed in practical charity towards our neighbors.

items.text: Have I failed to be kind and considerate to everyone I meet?
items.clarification: St. Francis said, 'When you encounter your neighbor, think, "God has created this person to love me, and me to love them."'

items.text: Have I spoken unkindly about others in their absence?
items.clarification: St. Francis strongly condemned detraction (speaking ill of others).

items.text: Have I judged others harshly in my thoughts?
Have I neglected to help those in need when I could have done so?
Have I been impatient with the faults and limitations of others?
Have I failed to forgive someone who has hurt me?
Have I neglected the needs of my family members?
Have I failed to treat others with respect and dignity as children of God?
Have I been overly critical or complaining?
Have I been unwilling to bear with the shortcomings of others charitably?

categories.title: Simplicity and Truthfulness
categories.description: St. Francis valued simplicity of life and truthfulness in all things.

items.text: Have I been dishonest or insincere in my words or actions?
items.clarification: St. Francis taught that 'a heart that loves God loves simplicity.'

items.text: Have I embellished stories or exaggerated to make myself look better?
Have I been artificial in my behavior, trying to impress others?
Have I spent too much time worrying about appearances and what others think?
Have I been overly attached to possessions or comforts?
Have I been wasteful or extravagant?
Have I lived beyond my means or been irresponsible with resources?
Have I failed to be grateful for what I have?

categories.title: Fulfillment of Daily Duties
categories.description: St. Francis taught that holiness is found in fulfilling our daily responsibilities with love and attention.

items.text: Have I neglected my responsibilities at home, work, or school?
items.clarification: St. Francis emphasized sanctification through our ordinary duties: 'Bloom where you are planted.'

items.text: Have I carried out my work without attention or care?
Have I wasted time that should have been devoted to my responsibilities?
Have I neglected to serve my family with love and patience?
Have I failed to balance work with proper rest and recreation?
Have I been lazy or procrastinated in important matters?
Have I neglected to develop my talents and abilities?
Have I failed to offer up difficulties and challenges to God?

categories.title: Interior Peace and Trust
categories.description: St. Francis emphasized maintaining a peaceful heart amidst the challenges of life.

items.text: Have I allowed worry, anxiety, or fear to dominate my thoughts?
items.clarification: St. Francis said, 'Do not lose your inner peace for anything whatsoever, even if your whole world seems upset.'

items.text: Have I failed to trust in God's providence in difficult circumstances?
Have I responded to challenges with impatience rather than calm trust?
Have I given way to discouragement or despair?
Have I allowed my emotions to control me rather than maintaining self-discipline?
Have I cultivated resentment or bitterness over past hurts?
Have I spent excessive time worrying about the future instead of trusting God?
Have I allowed busyness and haste to replace calm and mindfulness?

categories.title: Spiritual Joy and Contentment
categories.description: St. Francis emphasized joy as a hallmark of authentic devotion.

items.text: Have I failed to cultivate a spirit of joy and gratitude?
items.clarification: St. Francis said, 'A sad saint would be a sorry saint.'

items.text: Have I given in to a spirit of complaint or negativity?
Have I failed to notice and appreciate God's gifts in daily life?
Have I spread discouragement rather than encouragement to others?
Have I dwelled on past mistakes instead of accepting God's forgiveness?
Have I allowed envy to rob me of contentment with what I have?
Have I focused more on problems than on blessings?
Have I allowed myself to become overly serious or rigid in my spiritual life?

categories.title: Moderation and Self-Control
categories.description: St. Francis advocated balanced living and moderation in all things.

items.text: Have I been immoderate in eating, drinking, or entertainment?
items.clarification: St. Francis recommended balance, not extremes: 'A moderation which leans toward kindness is always preferable to one which leans toward severity.'

items.text: Have I acted impulsively without proper reflection?
Have I wasted time with excessive social media, television, or internet use?
Have I been overly rigid or scrupulous in my spiritual practices?
Have I neglected proper care for my physical health?
Have I failed to practice detachment from material goods and comforts?
Have I given in to laziness or excessive comfort-seeking?
Have I neglected to balance work with proper rest and recreation?

categories.title: Spiritual Direction and Growth
categories.description: St. Francis emphasized the importance of spiritual guidance and continuous growth.

items.text: Have I been closed to guidance or spiritual direction?
items.clarification: St. Francis highly valued spiritual direction, saying, 'Everyone needs a guide to lead them in the spiritual life.'

items.text: Have I neglected opportunities for spiritual growth or learning?
Have I been unwilling to examine my conscience regularly and honestly?
Have I resisted making necessary changes in my life?
Have I been complacent in my spiritual life, not striving to grow in virtue?
Have I neglected to read Scripture or spiritual books that would help me grow?
Have I failed to prepare properly for the sacrament of Confession?
Have I made excuses for my faults rather than working to overcome them?
